title: Blijf in het Nederlands
summary: Holding the line when the Dutch switch to English on you

blocks.title: The switch is kindness, not a verdict
blocks.body: Here's the thing every learner in the Netherlands hits: you open your mouth in careful Dutch, and the other person answers in **perfect English**. It stings. But hear this — they are being *helpful*, not judging you. They're trying to make it easy. The problem is that easy for them = no practice for you. So this lesson is one skill: **staying in Dutch, warmly, without making it awkward.** You are allowed to.
blocks.callout: Their English is a kindness. Your Dutch is a choice. You get to make it.

blocks.title: Phrases to hold the line
blocks.body: Keep these ready. They're short, polite, and they *invite* the other person to stay in Dutch with you instead of demanding it.

rows: Mag ik het in het Nederlands proberen?
May I try it in Dutch?
We kunnen Nederlands blijven praten, hoor.
We can keep speaking Dutch, really.
Can you speak a bit slower?

items.nl: Mag ik het in het Nederlands proberen?
items.en: May I try it in Dutch?
items.speak: Mag ik het in het Nederlands proberen?

items.nl: Hoe zeg je dat ook alweer?
items.en: How do you say that again?
items.speak: Hoe zeg je dat ook alweer?

items.nl: We kunnen Nederlands blijven praten, hoor.
items.en: We can keep it in Dutch, really.
items.speak: We kunnen Nederlands blijven praten, hoor.

blocks.title: The strategy when they switch to English
blocks.body: Three calm moves, in order. **1. Just keep going in Dutch.** Often they mirror you back within a sentence or two — no comment needed. **2. Name it lightly:** *'Ik oefen graag, mag het in het Nederlands?'* Nobody refuses that. **3. Trade, don't freeze:** take the English word they gave you, then continue in Dutch — *'Ah, invoice, dus de factuur. Oké, en dan…'* You lose nothing and you stay in the language.
blocks.callout: You never have to apologise for wanting to learn. Vragen staat vrij.

pairs.note: The pause is not failure. *Even denken* buys you time and sounds fluent.

pairs.right: Mag ik het in het Nederlands proberen?
pairs.note: Don't apologise your way out — invite yourself in. Positive framing keeps you in the driver's seat.
Asking to repeat is what confident speakers do, in any language.

blocks.prompt: Je hebt een hele zin gemist — te snel. Wat is de beste zet om in het Nederlands te blijven?
options: Kun je dat herhalen, iets langzamer?
blocks.explain: Asking to repeat — slower — keeps you in Dutch AND gets you the sentence. Nodding along teaches you nothing; switching to English ends the practice.

blocks.prompt: De verkoper antwoordt je in het Engels. Wat is de lichtste manier om vol te houden?
options: Say nothing and switch to English too
We kunnen Nederlands blijven praten, hoor.
blocks.explain: Warm, no blame, ends in *hoor* to soften it. Insulting their English (option 2) is both rude and wrong — theirs is great, that's the whole problem!

blocks.prompt: Typ de zin waarmee je vraagt hoe je iets zegt ('how do you say…?').
blocks.hint: Your most-used repair phrase. zeg = say.
blocks.explain: *Hoe zeg je…?* — reach for it the instant a word goes missing, instead of reaching for English.

blocks.prompt: Typ de twee woorden die je even bedenktijd geven ('Let me think…').
blocks.explain: *Even denken…* — the fluent-sounding pause. Silence feels long to you and normal to them.

blocks.scene: You told Emma you want to speak only Dutch today. Old habits kick in — and you hold the line.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Emma, ik wil vandaag alleen Nederlands praten. Mag dat?
lines.en: Emma, I want to speak only Dutch today. Is that okay?
lines.spotlight: You set the frame first — the strongest move of all.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.spotlight: And there it is — the reflex switch to English.

lines.speaker: You
lines.spotlight: Named it lightly, softened with hoor. No awkwardness.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.nl: Ah, sorry! Je hebt gelijk. Wat wil je drinken?
lines.en: Ah, sorry! You're right. What do you want to drink?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Even denken… een kopje thee, alsjeblieft.
lines.en: Let me think… a cup of tea, please.
lines.spotlight: even denken buys the pause; the diminutive keeps it cosy.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.nl: Zie je wel? Dat gaat hartstikke goed.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Dank je. Kun je iets langzamer praten? Dan versta ik je beter.
lines.en: Thanks. Can you speak a bit slower? Then I understand you better.
lines.spotlight: Asking for slower — a confident request, not an apology.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.nl: Natuurlijk, joh. Ik ben trots op je.
lines.en: Of course, mate. I'm proud of you.

blocks.title: Build your go-to line
blocks.prompt: Bouw de zin die de deur opent om in het Nederlands te blijven.
blocks.sample: Mag ik het in het Nederlands proberen?

blocks.prompt: Welke zin wordt jouw anker als iemand de volgende keer op Engels overschakelt? Schrijf hem op, en schrijf er één regel bij over de situatie waarin je hem gaat gebruiken.
